title: 大阪都構想「なぜ3回も」「副首都に」　見えた「市民の分断」
extracted_text: 地域政党「大阪維新の会」の大阪市議団が5月議会で大阪都構想への対応を決める参考にしようと、4月から始めたタウンミーティング（TM）がヤマ場を迎えている。 TMは4月5日から5月7日までの間、市内全24区で開催。100～200人程度を収容できる公共施設などであり、一部は座席数を超える市民が来場するなど関心も高い。 大阪市を廃止して特別区に再編する都構想は過去2回の住民投票で反対が上回ったものの、賛成と拮抗（きっこう）。「大阪を分断した」と言われており、今回のTMも会場で双方の意見が飛び交う。 都構想は大阪府が広域開発などを担い、大阪市が廃止された後の特別区が住民に身近なサービスを担う。府と市で似たような事業をする「二重行政」が防げるとされるが、開発に関する財源は市から府に移る。 反対する人たちからは「2度否決されたことをなぜ3回もしようとするのか」「特別区で財源を失い、住民サービスが低下するのでは」などの意見が出ている。 一方で「大阪が副首都になれば府が府内全域の広域行政を受け持つべきで、必要な構想だ」といった賛成意見も。具体的な制度案は府市でつくる「法定協議会（法定協）」で話し合われるため、早急に設置して明確なメリット、デメリットを公表すべきだとの声もある。 大阪維新代表の吉村洋文・大阪府知事は来春の統一地方選までに3度目となる住民投票を実施したい考え。代表代行の横山英幸・大阪市長も5月市議会に法定協設置に必要な議案を提出する構えだ。
translated_text: Osaka Restoration, a regional party with the Osaka City Council faction, has been holding town meetings (TMs) since April to gauge public opinion ahead of their decision on the Osaka Metropolis plan at the May assembly, and the series is now reaching its peak. TMs are being held from April 5 to May 7 across all 24 wards of the city, in public facilities that can typically accommodate 100–200 people. Some sessions have drawn overflow crowds, reflecting strong public interest. The Osaka Metropolis plan would abolish Osaka City and reorganize it into special wards. Although previous referendum votes twice rejected the plan, theyes were nearly tied. The issue has been blamed for "dividing Osaka," and the current TMs are no different, with both sides clashing at venues. Under the plan, Osaka Prefecture would handle broad-area development, while the special wards established after the city's abolition would provide services closer to residents. Proponents say it would eliminate "dual administration," where prefecture and city carry out similar programs. However, development funding would shift from the city to the prefecture. Opponents argue, "Why push for a third vote after being rejected twice?" and "Special wards will lose funding, and resident services will suffer." On the other hand, supporters say, "If Osaka becomes a sub-capital, the prefecture should manage broad-area administration across the entire prefecture—this is a necessary plan." Some voices call for promptly establishing the "Statutory Council" where specific institutional details would be negotiated between prefecture and city, so that clear pros and cons can be made public. Osaka Restoration leader and Osaka Prefecture Governor Hirofumi Yoshimura wants to hold the third referendum before next spring's unified local elections. Acting leader and Osaka Mayor Hideyuki Yokohama is also poised to submit the necessary ordinance to the May city assembly to establish the Statutory Council.
title_en: 'Why a Third Vote?' 'Sub-Capital?' Osaka Metropolis Plan Exposes City Divide
